diocese: The Episcopal Diocese of New York
sourceFile: PDF fetched directly from https://dioceseny.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/2026-Calendar-of-Intercession.pdf (12 pages), extracted with pdftotext -layout and visually cross-checked against a rendered page image (pdftoppm -png -r 150) to confirm the single-column layout.
notes: Genuinely a full calendar-year 2026 DAILY cycle (365 entries, one per calendar day Jan 1 - Dec 31), not weekly, per the source's own title "Calendar of Intercession" -- confirmed by counting 365 distinct "Month D, 2026" date lines in the extracted text, matching the non-leap 2026 calendar exactly. Unlike the corpus's other 365-entry precedent (episcopal-new-jersey-2026.json), this source's own layout is a clean single-column table (one date, one line of text) confirmed by visually rendering page 1 as an image and comparing it directly against the pdftotext -layout extraction -- no column-interleaving risk was found, and the four wrapped (two-line) entries in the raw text (Jan 27, Feb 10, Mar 10, Apr 25 -- each a bishop's consecration-anniversary entry whose sentence ran past one line) were confirmed to join correctly into a single entry by their position and by the rendered page.

Each day names exactly one subject in the source (never multiple congregations grouped under one date), so `subjects` has length 1 for every entry except December 28 (see below). Subject `type` was assigned per this corpus's schema rule (parish = a specific congregation with a given town/city; category = anything else, including diocesan offices/committees/commissions, named ministries, religious orders/communities, schools, chaplaincies, retreat/conference centers, bishops named on their consecration anniversaries, and named civic/diocesan observance days) -- this required a judgment call on essentially every entry, since the source itself does not label which of these its entries are. Ambiguous or borderline calls are on the specific dates disclosed below; the great majority of entries were unambiguous (a clear "Church Name, Town" pattern for parishes, or a clear office/committee/ministry sentence for categories).

`liturgicalNote` is left null on every entry. This source's own calendar is diocesan-content-driven, not keyed to the Church's liturgical calendar -- none of the eight liturgical observance days this corpus otherwise looks for (Ash Wednesday, Palm/Passion Sunday, Maundy Thursday, Good Friday, Holy Saturday, Easter Sunday, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day) is actually labeled as such anywhere in the source (e.g. Ash Wednesday, Feb 18, 2026, is printed as "Episcopal Relief and Development"; Easter Sunday, Apr 5, as "Hospice Chaplains of the Diocese"; Christmas Day, Dec 25, as "The Church of the Holy Nativity, Bronx" -- an ordinary parish day). A handful of dates DO name civic/diocesan observances as their sole content ("The Eve of Holocaust Remembrance Day", Jan 26; "Absalom Jones Observance", Feb 13; "Solemn day of remembrance of the attack on Pearl Harbor", Dec 7; the Sept 11 entry) -- these are transcribed as `category` subjects using the source's own text as `name`, not promoted to `liturgicalNote`, since they are not among this corpus's established set of labeled liturgical dates and the source does not print them as a label attached to some other subject (the observance IS the day's only content).

January 1 and April 21 both print "[The ]Congregation of St. Saviour at the Cathedral Church of St. John the Divine" (Jan 1 has the leading "The", Apr 21 does not -- both preserved exactly as printed) -- recorded as `category`, since no town/city is separately given (only "at the Cathedral Church of St. John the Divine", which is not itself a place name) and it is unclear whether this is meant as a distinct parish-like congregation or a ministry housed at the Cathedral.

January 3, "Community at the Crossing, Cathedral of St. John the Divine", is `category` for the same reason -- "Cathedral of St. John the Divine" after the comma is not a town/city, so it does not fit the parish subject shape's required `place` field.

January 19, "St. Peter's Church, Lithgow, Millbrook" (two commas), is a judgment call: transcribed as a `parish` subject with name "St. Peter's Church, Lithgow" (Lithgow being part of this specific congregation's own printed name, a hamlet in the Town of Millbrook) and place "Millbrook" (the town). This splits the source's own comma-separated text differently than every other single-comma parish line in this file; disclosed rather than silently resolved.

January 23, "The 2026 Learning Pilgrims to Cuernavaca, Mexico", is `category` despite ending in a real place name -- it names a diocesan pilgrimage group, not a congregation, so "Cuernavaca, Mexico" is the pilgrimage's destination, not this subject's own town.
January 27's source text reads "The. Rt. Rev. Catherine S. Roskam..." -- an apparent stray period after "The", preserved exactly as printed rather than silently corrected to "The Rt. Rev."

February 1 ("St John's Church (Tuckahoe), Yonkers") and November 16 ("St Margaret's Church (Longwood), Bronx") both print "St" without a period, unlike the great majority of this file's other "St." abbreviations -- preserved exactly as printed in each case, not normalized to match the file's more common style.

A number of entries that end in a real New York place name are nonetheless `category`, not `parish`, because the named entity is a school, nursery school, chaplaincy, retreat/conference center, or similar institution/ministry rather than itself a congregation (per this corpus's parish/category distinction, which requires the type-`parish` subject to be "a specific congregation"): e.g. "Christ's Church Nursery School, Rye" (Feb 8), "Sunset Nursery School, Montrose" (Jul 21), "The Day School at Christ and St. Stephens, Manhattan" (Aug 2), "St. Thomas Choir School, Manhattan" (Aug 3), "St. Luke's School, Manhattan" (Aug 9), "St. Philip's Nursery School, Garrison" (Aug 11), "The Eliza Corwin Frost Child Center of Christ Church, Bronxville" (Aug 12), "Grace Church School, Manhattan" (Aug 17), "Jack and Jill School at St. George's Church, Manhattan" (Aug 20), "Resurrection Episcopal Day School, Manhattan" (Aug 21), "St. Hilda's and St. Hugh's School, Manhattan" (Aug 22), "Canterbury Uptown Chaplaincy, Manhattan" (Sep 6), "Canterbury Downtown Chaplaincy, Manhattan" (Sep 19), "Episcopal Chaplaincy at the United States Military Academy, West Point" (Jul 3), and "Trinity School, Manhattan" (Jul 16, a school, distinct from any parish of the same/similar name). These are kept as `category` subjects with the source's full printed text as `name`, not split into a parish+place pair.

June 27, "The Haitian Congregation of the Good Samaritan, Bronx", IS recorded as `parish` (name "The Haitian Congregation of the Good Samaritan", place "Bronx") since it names a specific worshipping congregation, unlike the school/chaplaincy entries above.

May 24 prints "The Church Club Of New York" (capital "Of") while April 8 prints "Church Club of New York" (lowercase "of") -- two different capitalizations of what is evidently the same organization's name across two entries; both preserved exactly as printed, not normalized to match each other.

February 18 prints "Episcopal Relief and Development" while December 15 prints "Episcopal Relief & Development" -- the same organization named with "and" spelled out on one date and ampersanded on the other; both preserved exactly as printed.

July 10, "Trinity Retreat Center in West Cornwall Connecticut", is missing a comma before "Connecticut" (contrast with the file's many correctly comma-separated Town, State-less NY entries) -- preserved exactly as printed, treated as `category` (a retreat center, not a congregation).

November 25, "Vergers, Acolyles, Servers, Chalice Bearers, and Ushers of the Diocese" -- "Acolyles" is an apparent misspelling of "Acolytes", preserved exactly as printed rather than silently corrected.

December 28, "The Church of the Holy Innocents, Highland Falls/St Mark's Chapel, Fort Montgomery", names two distinct congregations in two distinct towns (Highland Falls and Fort Montgomery) joined by a slash on a single line -- unlike every other slash-joined "yoked parish" entry in this file, which shares a single place after one comma (e.g. April 23's "Calvary/St George's Church, Manhattan", June 17's "Parish of Trinity Church/St Paul's Chapel, Manhattan", November 15's "St. John's Church/St. Paul's Chapel, South Salem", all recorded as a single parish with one shared place). Because this entry genuinely names two different towns, it does not fit that same single-parish pattern; rather than guess at a split, it is kept as ONE `category` subject with the source's full text verbatim as `name`.

August 23 ("St. Bartholomew's Church, Manhattan") and August 24 ("St. Bartholomew's Church, White Plains") print the same congregation name for two different towns on consecutive days -- transcribed as printed with no correction; the source's cycle draws from roughly 200+ parishes across 365 days, so most congregations recur at least once and some names (St. Paul's, St. Andrew's, St. John's, Christ Church, Grace Church, etc.) are shared by multiple distinct congregations in different towns throughout the diocese -- this repetition and name-sharing is the source's own ordinary structure, not flagged individually beyond this note.

Every `parish` subject's `place` is exactly the town/borough the source prints after the entry's final comma (e.g. "Manhattan", "Bronx", "Staten Island" for New York City congregations, and the specific Hudson Valley/Westchester town for others); every `category` subject's `name` is the source's full line verbatim, since a diocesan office, committee, commission, school, ministry, religious order, or observance day does not carry a `place` field under this schema.
